subject: Biology
title: Inheritance
learningOutcomes: Define genetics, gene, allele, genotype, phenotype, homozygous and heterozygous; describe chromosomes, chromatids, centromere and nucleosomes.
Describe the central dogma and the role of a gene in protein synthesis (transcription and translation).
State and demonstrate Mendel's laws of segregation (3:1) and independent assortment (9:3:3:1).
Explain complete dominance, incomplete dominance (Japanese 4 O'Clock) and co-dominance (ABO blood groups).
Describe the sources of variation, continuous and discontinuous variation, natural selection and artificial selection.

sections.heading: Genes, Chromosomes & Chromatin
sections.body: Inheritance is the transfer of characters from parents to offspring; genetics is the study of inheritance and variations. Characters are controlled by genes — segments of DNA that code for proteins. Genes lie on thread-like chromosomes (discovered by Waldeyer in 1876); each chromosome has two chromatids joined at the centromere. Chromatin is DNA only in prokaryotes and DNA + histones in eukaryotes, where DNA wrapped around histones forms nucleosomes — 'beads on a string' that coil into a chromosome.

sections.heading: Gene, Allele & Genetic Terms
sections.body: An allele is an alternative form of a gene; the location of a gene is its locus. The genotype is the combination of alleles of a gene pair — homozygous (same alleles) or heterozygous (different alleles). The phenotype is the observable outcome. A dominant allele (capital letter) masks the recessive allele (lowercase letter) in a heterozygote.

sections.heading: Protein Synthesis & the Central Dogma
sections.body: Protein synthesis has two steps. In transcription the DNA strands unzip and one strand is the template for a single strand of mRNA. In translation the mRNA travels to the ribosome, tRNA brings amino acids, and the amino acids are linked into a protein. The central dogma is DNA → RNA → Protein.

sections.heading: Mendel's Laws
sections.body: Gregor Mendel (Father of Genetics) worked on the garden pea in 1856–1864. A monohybrid cross of true-breeding tall (TT) and short (tt) plants gives all tall Tt F1 plants; self-pollination gives a 3 tall : 1 short F2 ratio (1 TT : 2 Tt : 1 tt) — the law of segregation. A dihybrid cross RRYY × rryy gives RrYy F1 plants forming four gametes (RY, Ry, rY, ry) and a 9:3:3:1 F2 ratio from 16 combinations — the law of independent assortment.

sections.heading: Dominance Relations
sections.body: In complete dominance one allele fully masks the other (Tt is tall). In incomplete dominance the heterozygote is intermediate: in the Japanese 4 O'Clock plant RR is red, rr is white and Rr is pink; pink × pink gives 1 red : 2 pink : 1 white. In co-dominance both alleles are fully expressed: ABO blood groups are controlled by I^A, I^B and i — I^A I^A/I^A i = A, I^B I^B/I^B i = B, ii = O and I^A I^B = AB.

sections.heading: Variation, Evolution & Selection
sections.body: Variation is the difference in traits between individuals of the same species. Its sources are genetic recombination in meiosis, crossing over in prophase, random fertilization, mutation and environmental conditions. Continuous variation (height, skin colour) is controlled by many genes; discontinuous variation (blood groups, ear lobes) by a few. Darwin's natural selection — overproduction, competition, reproduction, speciation — drives organic evolution, e.g. pesticide-resistant flour beetles. In artificial selection people choose which plants and animals reproduce, producing breeds and cultivars.

definitions.definition: The process by which characters are transferred from parents to offspring.
The branch of biology that studies inheritance, variations and the factors controlling them.
A segment of DNA with a code for protein synthesis; the unit of heredity.
An alternative form of the same gene.
The location of a gene on a chromosome.
The combination of the alleles of a gene pair.
The observable outcome of a genotype, in the form of a characteristic.
A genotype in which the gene pair has the same alleles.
A genotype in which the gene pair has different alleles.
The allele that masks the working of the other allele in a heterozygous genotype.
The allele that is masked (not expressed) in a heterozygous genotype.
A thread-like structure in cells, composed of chromatin material, that carries genes.
One of the two identical halves of a chromosome.
The point at which the two chromatids of a chromosome are attached.
The material of which chromosomes are composed (DNA, with histone proteins in eukaryotes).
A protein around which the DNA is wrapped in eukaryotic chromatin.
The structure made of histones with the DNA wrapped around them.
The step in which one DNA strand is used as a template to make a single strand of mRNA.
The step in which tRNA brings amino acids to the ribosome and they are linked into a protein.
The RNA that carries the copied instructions of DNA from the nucleus to the ribosome.
The RNA that carries specific amino acids to the ribosome.
The flow of genetic information from DNA to RNA to protein.
The original true-breeding parental generation.
The first filial generation, the first set of offspring of the parents.
The second filial generation, produced by self-pollination of the F1 plants.
An F1 offspring of two parents with different characteristics.
The trait that dominates the phenotype in the F1 generation.
The trait that is masked by the dominant trait in the F1 generation.
A cross in which the inheritance of one character is studied at a time.
A cross in which the inheritance of two characters is studied at a time.
Genetically homozygous individuals that produce offspring with the same character.
Paired alleles separate during gamete formation and each gamete receives one allele, not both.
Alleles separate independently of one another during the formation of gametes.
One allele is completely dominant over the other allele.
An allele does not completely mask the other, so the heterozygote shows a blend of both phenotypes.
Different alleles of a gene are completely expressed together in the heterozygous condition.
Differences in traits between individuals of the same species.
The exchange of genes between chromatids of homologous chromosomes during prophase of meiosis.
Any change in the nucleotide sequence of DNA.
The original allele, before a mutation occurs.
The new allele produced by a mutation.
Variation with a wide range of phenotypes and many intermediates, controlled by many genes.
Variation with only a few clear-cut phenotypes and no intermediates, controlled by a few genes.
The development of advanced types of organisms from pre-existing simpler and imperfect forms by gradual modification.
The process in which individuals with better variations produce more surviving offspring than those lacking them.
The tendency of organisms to produce more offspring than the environment can support.
The struggle among organisms for the limited resources of the environment.
The process in which a population changes entirely over many generations and new species may evolve.
The process in which people allow only plants and animals with desirable characteristics to reproduce.
The varieties of artificially bred animals.
The varieties of artificially bred plants.

examTips: Learn the 3:1 (monohybrid) and 9:3:3:1 (dihybrid) ratios — and which of Mendel's laws each one proves.
Draw the Punnett square: Tt × Tt gives 1 TT : 2 Tt : 1 tt (genotype) but 3 tall : 1 short (phenotype).
Incomplete dominance = intermediate (pink); co-dominance = both alleles expressed (AB blood group).
Blood groups: I^A I^A or I^A i = A; I^B I^B or I^B i = B; ii = O; I^A I^B = AB. A heterozygous-by-heterozygous A × B cross can give O.
Natural selection steps in order: overproduction → competition → reproduction → speciation.
Continuous variation = many genes, wide range (height); discontinuous = few genes, clear-cut classes (blood groups).

practiceQuestions.prompt: The branch of biology that studies inheritance, variations and the factors controlling them is:
practiceQuestions.explanation: Genetics studies inheritance, variations and the factors controlling them.
A gene is a segment of DNA that codes for a protein.

practiceQuestions.prompt: The structure formed when DNA is wrapped around histone proteins is called a:
practiceQuestions.explanation: DNA wrapped around histones forms a nucleosome (beads on a string).

practiceQuestions.prompt: The different forms of a gene for the same trait are called:
practiceQuestions.explanation: Alternative forms of a gene are alleles.

practiceQuestions.prompt: The central dogma is best represented by:
practiceQuestions.explanation: Genetic information flows DNA → RNA → Protein.

practiceQuestions.prompt: Who is regarded as the Father of Genetics?
practiceQuestions.explanation: Gregor Mendel, an Austrian monk, worked on the garden pea (1856–1864).

practiceQuestions.prompt: How many different types of gametes are produced by a plant of genotype AaBb?
practiceQuestions.explanation: AaBb forms AB, Ab, aB and ab — four types.

practiceQuestions.prompt: The I^A and I^B alleles of the ABO system follow which dominance pattern?
practiceQuestions.explanation: Both I^A and I^B are expressed together in I^A I^B (blood group AB) — co-dominance.

practiceQuestions.prompt: In a Tt × Tt cross, what is the F2 phenotypic ratio (tall : short)?
practiceQuestions.explanation: 1 TT : 2 Tt : 1 tt gives 3 tall : 1 short.

practiceQuestions.prompt: Natural selection operates to produce changes in:
practiceQuestions.explanation: Natural selection changes populations over time.

practiceQuestions.prompt: In incomplete dominance the heterozygote shows an intermediate phenotype.
practiceQuestions.explanation: True — e.g. Rr gives pink flowers in the Japanese 4 O'Clock plant.

practiceQuestions.prompt: Human blood groups are an example of continuous variation.
practiceQuestions.explanation: False — blood groups (A, B, AB, O) are discontinuous variation.

practiceQuestions.prompt: Crossing over occurs during the prophase of meiosis.
practiceQuestions.explanation: True — chromatids of homologous chromosomes exchange genes.

practiceQuestions.prompt: In protein synthesis, DNA is copied into mRNA in the step called _____.
practiceQuestions.explanation: Transcription copies a DNA strand into mRNA.

practiceQuestions.prompt: The varieties of animals that are artificially bred are called _____.
practiceQuestions.explanation: Artificially bred animal varieties are breeds; plant varieties are cultivars.

sequencingActivity.prompt: Arrange the steps of natural selection in the correct order:
sequencingActivity.explanation: Natural selection works through overproduction → competition → reproduction → speciation.

bossBattleQuestions.prompt: Two tall pea plants produce a short offspring (T = tall, t = short). What are the genotypes of the parents?
bossBattleQuestions.explanation: A tt offspring needs a t from each parent; both tall parents are therefore Tt.

bossBattleQuestions.prompt: A man with blood group AB marries a woman with blood group O. Which blood groups can their children have?
bossBattleQuestions.explanation: I^A I^B × ii gives 50% I^A i (A) and 50% I^B i (B); no AB and no O children.

bossBattleQuestions.prompt: Two pink-flowered Japanese 4 O'Clock plants are crossed. Out of 400 offspring, how many are expected to be pink?
bossBattleQuestions.explanation: Rr × Rr gives 1 RR : 2 Rr : 1 rr = 1 red : 2 pink : 1 white; half (200) are pink.

bossBattleQuestions.prompt: Out of 1600 F2 plants from RrYy × RrYy (round yellow dominant), how many are expected to be wrinkled and green?
Survivors of the first pesticide sprays had variations for resistance and passed them on, so resistant flour beetles increased in each generation. This is an example of:
bossBattleQuestions.explanation: The environment (pesticide) selected resistant variations — natural selection.
